title: Vertical sections contract augmented comma bar complexes
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ and $s:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors between small categories in [def-weil-size-convention], with $us=1_{\mathcal D}$, and let $\eta:1_{\mathcal E}\Rightarrow su$ satisfy $u(\eta_U)=1_{uU}$ for every $U$. Give the categories the identity-cover topology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $K:\mathcal D^{op}\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ a module presheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $V\in\mathcal D$, let $\mathcal I_V=(V\downarrow u)$ have objects $(U,a:V\to uU)$ and arrows $h:(U,a)\to(U',a')$ with $u(h)a=a'$. Put $F_V(U,a)=K(uU)$. Let $\mathcal J_V=(V\downarrow\mathcal D)$, with $H_V(W,a)=K(W)$, and define $p(U,a)=(uU,a)$, $s_V(W,a)=(sW,a)$. On the category bar complexes of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] the induced chain maps satisfy
$$K(p)K(s_V)=1,\qquad K(s_V)K(p)\simeq1.$$
They preserve the augmentations to $K(V)[0]$ whose degree-zero formulas are $((U,a),x)\mapsto K(a)x$ and $((W,a),x)\mapsto K(a)x$, respectively. The latter augmentation is a chain homotopy equivalence with inverse the degree-zero inclusion at $(V,1_V)$ and zero in the other degrees. Consequently the specified augmentation $K_{\mathcal I_V}(F_V)\to K(V)[0]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence, with inverse the degree-zero inclusion at $(sV,1_V)$; all assertions are natural in $K$. Here $\simeq$ means chain homotopy, and $M[0]$ is the complex with $M$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere.
The augmentation conclusion also holds with coherent identifications in place of $us=1$: suppose $\epsilon:us\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal D}$ is a natural isomorphism and $\epsilon_{uU}\circ u(\eta_U)=1_{uU}$. Then take $s_V(W,a)=(sW,\epsilon_W^{-1}a)$ and coefficient map $K(\epsilon_W):K(W)\to K(usW)$ for its bar map. The augmentation inverse in this case includes at $(sV,\epsilon_V^{-1})$ using $K(\epsilon_V)$.

proof.text: Write $C_I=K_{\mathcal I_V}(F_V)$ and $C_J=K_{\mathcal J_V}(H_V)$. On arrows $F_V(h)=K(u(h))$. The relation $u(h)a=a\prime$ gives $K(a)K(u(h))=K(a\prime)$; hence the proposed degree-zero maps are cocones. By the displayed bar differential their composites with $d:C^{-1}\to C^0$ vanish, so they define chain maps $A_I:C_I\to K(V)[0]$ and $A_J:C_J\to K(V)[0]$. Smallness is inherited by the comma categories (objects and arrows are subsets of products of the given small sets), so every bar sum is permitted.

proof.text: First suppose $us=1$. The functors $p,s_V$ act on arrows by $u,s$, and $ps_V=1$. Since $F_V=p^{-1}H_V$ and $s_V^{-1}F_V=H_V$, the cited reindexing formula defines $P=K(p,1)$ and $B=K(s_V,1)$ and gives $PB=1$. The arrows $\eta_U:(U,a)\to(suU,a)$ form a natural transformation $1_{\mathcal I_V}\Rightarrow s_Vp$: the comma condition is $u(\eta_U)a=a$ and naturality is that of $\eta$. For this transformation, with $G=F_V$ and coefficient map $t=1$, the coefficient restriction is $F_V(\eta_U)=K(1_{uU})=1$. The natural-transformation clause of the cited node therefore gives $BP\simeq1$. The generator formulas also give $A_JP=A_I$ and $A_IB=A_J$.

proof.text: Let $T=(V,1_V)$ in $\mathcal J_V$. Its unique arrow to $(W,a)$ is $a$, so $T$ is initial. Define $i:K(V)[0]\to C_J$ by degree-zero inclusion at $T$ and zero elsewhere; $A_Ji=1$. For $n\ge0$ define $S_n:C_J^{-n}\to C_J^{-n-1}$ by $(X_n\to\cdots\to X_0,x)\mapsto(T\to X_n\to\cdots\to X_0,x)$. Using the cited face convention, $d_0S_n=1$, $d_jS_n=S_{n-1}d_{j-1}$ for $n\ge1$, $1\le j\le n+1$ (including the coefficient face), while $d_1S_0=iA_J$. The alternating sum gives $dS+Sd=1$ in negative degrees and $dS_0=1-iA_J$ in degree zero. Thus $iA_J\simeq1$ and $A_J$ is the asserted chain homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: In the strict case put $b=Bi$. The identities already proved give $A_Ib=A_Ji=1$. Whisker the homotopy $iA_J\simeq1$ by $B,P$: then $bA_I=BiA_JP\simeq BP\simeq1$. On degree zero $b$ includes at $(sV,1_V)$, and its other components vanish. This proves the specified inverse, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories), and lemma-initial-final; explicit section and coefficient refinement by Q99 of cotangent.tex Tag 08QW (lemma-triangle-compute-lower-shriek), cases i=1,2.

proof.text: Now let $\epsilon:us\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ be as stated. Keep $p$ and put $s_V(W,a)=(sW,\epsilon_W^{-1}a)$, with arrow map $s$. Naturality of $\epsilon^{-1}$ verifies its comma condition. Set $B=K(s_V,t)$ with $t_{(W,a)}=K(\epsilon_W)$; naturality of $\epsilon$ makes $t$ a natural coefficient map $H_V\to s_V^{-1}F_V$. There is a natural transformation $\alpha:ps_V\Rightarrow1_{\mathcal J_V}$ with component $\epsilon_W$, so the cited bar homotopy gives $PB=K(ps_V,H_V(\alpha))\simeq1$. There is also $\beta:1_{\mathcal I_V}\Rightarrow s_Vp$ with component $\eta_U$: its comma condition follows from $u(\eta_U)=\epsilon_{uU}^{-1}$. For its coefficient map $t\prime_{(U,a)}=K(\epsilon_{uU})$ one has $F_V(\beta_U)t\prime_U=K(u(\eta_U))K(\epsilon_{uU})=1$. The cited natural-transformation clause and composition formula give $BP=K(s_Vp,t\prime)\simeq1$.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories), and lemma-initial-final; explicit section and coefficient refinement by Q99 of cotangent.tex Tag 08QW (lemma-triangle-compute-lower-shriek), cases i=1,2.

proof.text: Here $A_JP=A_I$ as before, and $A_IB=A_J$ because on a degree-zero generator its coefficient map is $K(\epsilon_W^{-1}a)K(\epsilon_W)=K(a)$. Hence $b=Bi$ again has $A_Ib=1$ and $bA_I=BiA_JP\simeq BP\simeq1$. Its degree-zero formula is inclusion at $(sV,\epsilon_V^{-1})$ with coefficient $K(\epsilon_V)$, exactly as asserted. For a natural module map $\theta:K\to L$, the equation $\theta_XK(f)=L(f)\theta_Y$ for $f:X\to Y$ shows that every coefficient formula above commutes with $\theta$. The insertion $S$ leaves coefficients unchanged. The homotopies $BP\simeq1$ and $PB\simeq1$ may be taken to be the explicit prism homotopies $H_n=\sum_r(-1)^rp_r$ of [lem-trf-coefficient-bar-prism-homotopy] for $(\beta,t')$ and $(\alpha,1)$; each $p_r$ inserts a component of $\eta$ or $\epsilon$ and applies the coefficient map $t'_{U_0}=K(\epsilon_{uU_0})$, resp. the identity, so it commutes with $\theta$. Thus the maps, contractions, and resulting assertions are natural in $K$.
